page: https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/migration-guides | "Migration guides" | section: migrate-from-llama/tokenizer

## section: migrate-from-llama/tokenizer
    Migration guides > Migrate from self-hosted Llama > Tokenizer
    cite: https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/migration-guides#migrate-from-llama
### Tokenizer

Mistral models use a different tokenizer than Llama. If you compute token counts manually or handle raw tokenization, update your tooling.

Install the official Mistral tokenizer:

```bash
pip install mistral-common
```

Use it to tokenize text:

```python
from mistral_common.tokens.tokenizers.mistral import MistralTokenizer

tokenizer = MistralTokenizer.v3()
result = tokenizer.encode_chat_completion(
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello, world!"}]
)
print(result.tokens)
```

Mistral models on Hugging Face are also compatible with the `transformers` library. Use `apply_chat_template` to handle formatting automatically.

2. Use it to tokenize text with `MistralTokenizer.v3()`
3. Example shows encoding chat completion messages

The key is to use `mistral-common` library with `MistralTokenizer.v3()`. To count tokens, you would encode your prompt and then get the length of the tokens array.

content.text:
Install the `mistral-common` package, then encode your prompt with `MistralTokenizer.v3()` and count the resulting tokens:

```bash
pip install mistral-common
```

```python
from mistral_common.tokens.tokenizers.mistral import MistralTokenizer
tokenizer = MistralTokenizer.v3()
result = tokenizer.encode_chat_completion(
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Your prompt here"}]
)
token_count = len(result.tokens)
```

[Migrate from self-hosted Llama > Tokenizer](https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/migration-guides#migrate-from-llama)
